newsitem.title: USA: SAIC agrees to buy Bellcore.
newsitem.headline: SAIC agrees to buy Bellcore.

text.p: Science Applications International Corp (SAIC) said Thursday it agreed to buy Bell Communications Research Inc (Bellcore), the research and engineering arm of the seven regional Bell companies.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Bellcore's board said early last year that Bellcore's owners were considering selling the company as a result of changing developments in the telecommunications industry and the owners' diverging strategies and business plans.
"Bellcore and SAIC are well positioned for the future," said SAIC chairman J. Robert Beyster.

"We envision serving new markets where our two companies can combine their considerable skills. These include large software projects, advanced network designs, secure networks, Internet technologies, wireless communications, and other advances in telecommunications software systems and technology," Beyster said.
The deal is expected to be finalized in late 1997 after Bellcore's owners obtain the requisite regulatory approvals, the companies said.

Bellcore, which was formed in 1984 as a research and engineering company supporting its seven owners, and provides communications software, engineering and consulting services. Morristown, N.J.-based Bellcore has 5,600 employees and annual revenues exceeding $1 billion.

Bellcore currently is owned by the Regional Bell Operating Companies, which include Ameritech Corp, Bell Atlantic Corp, BellSouth Corp, NYNEX Corp, Pacific Telesis Group, SBC Communications, and U S West Inc.
Employee-owned SAIC provides high technology products and services to government and private industry.
With annual revenues exceeding $2.2 billion, SAIC and its subsidiaries have 22,000 employees in more than 475 locations worldwide.
